post.description:
Ends the session server-side and clears the cookie.

Succeeds whether or not the request carried a usable session.

Sets a new password for the signed-in user, who must know the old one.

Every other session of the user is ended. This one continues, under a
new cookie.

Removes the signed-in user's account, at once and for good.

The password has to be given again: a session alone does not remove an
account. Whose account it is, is always the signed-in user's; there is
no way to name another.

With the account go its posts, stories, likes, reposts and follows, and
every session of it. A post that others have replied to leaves an empty
place in its thread, with no author and no text. The username and the
email address are free again from that moment.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Auth Sessions Get

get.description: The signed-in user's own profile, including the fields only they may see.

patch.description:
Changes the signed-in user's own profile and returns the result.

Only the fields that are sent are changed. The profile that is updated is
always the caller's; there is no way to name another user.

put.description:
Makes the uploaded picture the signed-in user's own, in place of the
one before, and returns the profile.

Sent as a form (multipart/form-data). The picture is decoded and drawn
again by the server as a 400 by 400 square cut from its middle, and
nothing of the uploaded file but its pixels is kept: no location, no
camera, no other metadata. The previous picture is removed.

delete.description:
Removes the signed-in user's picture, and returns the profile.

Removing a picture that is not there changes nothing and is not an error.

post.description:
Everything Hopsnop holds that is the signed-in user's own, as one ZIP
archive to download: a JSON document (`export.json`) and the user's
pictures, which the document names by their place in the archive.

The password has to be given again: a session alone does not hand out
all of an account's data. Whose data it is, is always the signed-in
user's; there is no way to name another.

The document holds no password, no token and no id of a session, and of
other people only what the user could already see: the usernames of
accounts they follow or are followed by, and the ids of posts and
stories they answered, liked, reposted or viewed.

It is not a snapshot of one moment. Its parts are read one after the
other, and each shows the user's data as it was when that part was
read. What the user does while the export is being made can be in one
part and not in another.

200.description: The archive: export.json and the pictures it names.

get.description:
A user's public profile. No authentication is needed.

`following` says whether the caller follows the user. It is false for an
anonymous request.

A user's current picture. No authentication is needed: it is part of
the public profile, and found under the same rules.

The address names the picture, so it is not reused: once the picture is
replaced or removed, the address answers `404`. A browser may keep its
copy for a day (`private`: no shared cache may).

A user's posts, newest first, replies included.

No authentication is needed.

post.description:
Makes the caller follow the user. Following takes effect at once.

Who follows is always the signed-in user; there is no way to name
another. Following a user who is already followed changes nothing and is
not an error.

delete.description:
Makes the caller no longer follow the user.

Unfollowing a user who is not followed changes nothing and is not an
error.

get.description:
Whether the caller follows the user. No authentication is needed.

An anonymous caller follows nobody, so the answer is then always false.

The users who follow the user, the most recent follower first.

No authentication is needed.

The users the user follows, the most recently followed first.

No authentication is needed.

post.description:
Publishes a post, or a reply if `parent_post_id` is given.

The author is always the signed-in user; there is no way to name another.

get.description:
A single post. No authentication is needed.

A post that was deleted, or whose author's account is not shown, is not
found.

patch.description:
Changes the text of the caller's own post and returns the result.

Possible for 60 minutes after the post was created.

get.description:
The replies to a post, newest first. No authentication is needed.

Only the replies to this post itself, not the replies to those. A post
that was deleted, or whose author's account is not shown, is not found.

post.description: Likes a post the caller can see.

delete.description: Takes the caller's like back from a post they can see.

post.description: Reposts a post the caller can see.

delete.description: Takes the caller's repost back from a post they can see.

get.description:
For You: every post that is shown, newest first, replies included.

No authentication is needed, and the same posts are in it with or without
it. Whom the caller follows plays no part.

Following: the posts of the users the caller follows, newest first,
replies included.

Whose feed it is, is always the signed-in user; there is no way to name
another.

post.description:
Publishes a story: an uploaded picture, with an optional caption.

Sent as a form (multipart/form-data). The picture is decoded and drawn
again by the server, at most 1440 pixels on its longer side, and nothing
of the uploaded file but its pixels is kept: no location, no camera, no
other metadata.

The author is always the signed-in user; there is no way to name another.
The story is shown for 24 hours.

get.description:
The active stories of the caller and of the users they follow, newest
first.

Reading the list records no views.

A single active story, the caller's own or of a user they follow.

Any other story is not found. Reading a story records no view.

delete.description:
Deletes the caller's own story, together with its views and its
picture.

get.description:
The picture of a story, to whoever may see the story and nobody else.

Always a WebP file made by the server. It is checked at every request
who may see it: a browser keeps a copy but asks again each time
(`no-cache`), and is told `304` only if the story is still shown to it.

post.description:
Records that the caller has viewed a story they can see.

Whose view it is, is always the signed-in user; there is no way to name
another. It can be repeated: a story is viewed by a user once, however
often this is called. An author's look at their own story is not a view.

AccountResponse.title: AccountResponse
AccountResponse.description:
A user as shown to that user.

It includes private fields such as the email address, so it must only be
returned to the account's owner.

image.title: Image
image.description: The picture: a JPEG, PNG or WebP file.

caption.title: Caption
caption.description: Up to 150 characters of plain text. Blank or absent for a story without one.

image.title: Image
image.description: The picture: a JPEG, PNG or WebP file.

parent_post_id.title: Parent Post Id
parent_post_id.description: The post this one replies to. null or absent for a new post.

DeleteAccountRequest.title: DeleteAccountRequest
DeleteAccountRequest.description:
Removing the caller's own account. The password is all it takes, and
all a client can say: which account it is, is the session's to tell.

ExportRequest.title: ExportRequest
ExportRequest.description:
Asking for one's own data. The password is all a client can say:
whose data it is, is the session's to tell.

FollowResponse.title: FollowResponse
FollowResponse.description: Whether the caller follows a user.

LikeResponse.title: LikeResponse
LikeResponse.description: Where a post stands with the caller's like after a request.

MyProfileResponse.title: MyProfileResponse
MyProfileResponse.description:
A user as shown to that user.

It includes private fields such as the email address, so it must only be
returned to the account's owner.

PostAuthorResponse.title: PostAuthorResponse
PostAuthorResponse.description: What a post shows of its author: enough to render a byline.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. null when there are no more posts.

PostPageResponse.title: PostPageResponse
PostPageResponse.description: One page of a list of posts, newest first.

PostResponse.title: PostResponse
PostResponse.description:
A post as shown to someone who may see it.

There is no deletion field: a deleted post is not returned at all.

PublicProfileResponse.title: PublicProfileResponse
PublicProfileResponse.description: A user as shown to anyone, signed in or not.

RepostResponse.title: RepostResponse
RepostResponse.description: Where a post stands with the caller's repost after a request.

StoryAuthorResponse.title: StoryAuthorResponse
StoryAuthorResponse.description:
What a story shows of its author: enough to render it and to link to
the profile, which is addressed by the username.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. null when there are no more stories.

StoryPageResponse.title: StoryPageResponse
StoryPageResponse.description: One page of a list of stories, newest first.

StoryResponse.title: StoryResponse
StoryResponse.description:
An active story as shown to someone who may see it.

A story that has expired or was deleted is not returned at all.

StoryViewResponse.title: StoryViewResponse
StoryViewResponse.description: Where a story stands with the caller's view after a request.

UpdatePostRequest.title: UpdatePostRequest
UpdatePostRequest.description: An edit of the caller's own post. The text is all that can change.

bio.title: Bio
bio.description: Up to 160 characters of plain text. null or blank clears it.

UpdateProfileRequest.title: UpdateProfileRequest
UpdateProfileRequest.description:
A partial update of the caller's own profile.

Only the fields that are sent are changed; a field that is left out keeps
its value. Sending ``null`` for ``bio`` clears it.

These two fields are the only ones a user can change here. Anything else
in the body is ignored, like everywhere else in the API. The picture is
changed by uploading one (``PUT /users/me/avatar``), not by naming it.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. null when there are no more users.

UserPageResponse.title: UserPageResponse
UserPageResponse.description: One page of a list of users.

UserSummaryResponse.title: UserSummaryResponse
UserSummaryResponse.description:
What a list of users shows of each.

Enough to render a row and to link to the profile, which is addressed by
the username. No id is needed for that, so there is none.
